title: Equivariant etale coordinates for a tame smooth morphism
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group of exponent dividing $N$, and let $\Lambda$ be the localization of $\mathbf Z[1/N,\zeta_N]$ at a prime, where $\zeta_N$ is a primitive $N$th root of unity. Let $h:X\to B$ be an equivariant smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of locally Noetherian $\Lambda$-schemes, with $G$ acting trivially on $\Lambda$. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ fixed by every element of $G$, in the sense that each element induces the identity on that geometric point. After equivariant pointed etale neighborhoods near this point and its image, there are a finite free $\Lambda$-module $V$ with a $\Lambda$-linear $G$-action and an equivariant etale $B$-morphism
$$c:X\longrightarrow B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda}\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Sym}_{\Lambda}(V).$$
Its projection to $B$ is $h$. Here etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism], finite free means having a finite basis, and $\operatorname{Sym}_{\Lambda}(V)$ is the commutative $\Lambda$-algebra generated by symbols $[v]$, subject to $[v+w]=[v]+[w]$ and $[av]=a[v]$. The action is the one induced from $V$. The module $V$ may have rank zero.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, second assertion and its proof, printed p.138, equations (4)--(5), followed by the localization of Lambda in 1.3, printed pp.139--140.

proof.text: Write $x$ for the underlying point, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $k=\kappa(x)$, and $D=k\otimes_R\Omega^1_{X/B,x}$. Every element of $G$ fixes $x$ and acts identically on $k$: the embedding of $k$ into the geometric residue field is injective and is fixed by the hypothesis on $\bar x$. Thus the actions on $R$ and $D$ are $\Lambda$-linear, and the action on $D$ is $k$-linear. The universal derivation $\delta:R\to D$ is equivariant (differentiate the equivariance of $h$). By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], the elements $\delta(f)$, $f\in R$, span $D$ over $k$. By [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free], $D$ has finite dimension. This uses relative differentials, without identifying them with a maximal-ideal quotient.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, second assertion, printed p.138, equations (4)--(5) and Jacobian criterion; localization of the coefficient ring in X 1.3, printed pp.139--140. Adaptation using relative differential generators at the given point.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-local-cyclotomic-group-algebra-split] to choose matrix units $E^i_{ab}\in\Lambda[G]$ for all its matrix factors, acting on $R$ and $D$. For each $i$, the vectors $E^i_{11}\delta(f)=\delta(E^i_{11}f)$ span $E^i_{11}D$ over $k$, since $G$ fixes $k$. Choose $f_{i\ell}\in R$ so that these vectors form a basis, with $1\leq\ell\leq m_i$; $m_i=0$ is permitted. Set $V=\bigoplus_i(\Lambda^{d_i})^{m_i}$, with its $\Lambda[G]$-action through the matrix decomposition, and define $\phi:V\to R$ by $\phi(e^i_{a\ell})=E^i_{a1}f_{i\ell}$. The identities $E^j_{bc}E^i_{a1}=0$ for $j\ne i$ and $E^i_{bc}E^i_{a1}=\delta_{ca}E^i_{b1}$ prove that $\phi$ is equivariant. The images of the standard basis under $\delta\phi$ form a $k$-basis of $D$: indeed $D=\bigoplus_{i,a}E^i_{aa}D$, and $E^i_{a1}:E^i_{11}D\to E^i_{aa}D$ has inverse $E^i_{1a}$. Consequently $k\otimes_\Lambda V\to D$ is an isomorphism. The displayed direct sum already gives a finite basis of $V$; no freeness theorem over local rings is needed.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, second assertion, printed p.138, equations (4)--(5) and Jacobian criterion; localization of the coefficient ring in X 1.3, printed pp.139--140. Adaptation using relative differential generators at the given point.

proof.text: There are finitely many functions $\phi(e^i_{a\ell})$ and finitely many equivariance identities, one for each $g\in G$ and basis vector. Represent the functions by sections on a common open neighbourhood of $x$. An equality of germs holds on a smaller open neighbourhood, so shrink once for each of these finitely many identities. Intersect all the translates of the resulting open: every translate contains $x$, and their finite intersection $U$ is open and $G$-stable. Restrictions of the sections then define an equivariant $\Lambda$-linear map $V\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. No affine intersection or invariant affine neighbourhood is assumed. Actions on functions use inverse pullback, so that they are left actions; all matrix-unit and equivariance identities use this convention.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, second assertion, printed p.138, equations (4)--(5) and Jacobian criterion; localization of the coefficient ring in X 1.3, printed pp.139--140. Adaptation using relative differential generators at the given point.

proof.text: The symmetric-algebra presentation in the statement extends this linear map uniquely to a $\Lambda$-algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}_\Lambda(V)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Together with $h|_U$ this defines $c:U\to B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda}\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Sym}_\Lambda(V)$ over $B$. Its equivariance is checked on constants and the generators $[v]$, where it is exactly the equivariance proved in Step 3. Choose the displayed finite basis of $V$; it identifies its symmetric algebra with a polynomial algebra, and the coordinate differentials of $c$ at $x$ are precisely the basis of $D$ from Step 2.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, second assertion, printed p.138, equations (4)--(5) and Jacobian criterion; localization of the coefficient ring in X 1.3, printed pp.139--140. Adaptation using relative differential generators at the given point.

proof.text: Take an affine standard smooth chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ for $h|_U$ at $x$, using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-locally-standard-smooth]. Write its presentation as $A=C[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_c)$ with the first $c$ by $c$ Jacobian minor invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{A/C}$ has basis $\mathrm dz_{c+1},\ldots,\mathrm dz_n$. Put $d=n-c=\dim_kD$, and lift the $d$ coordinate functions of $c$ to polynomials $H_1,\ldots,H_d\in C[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$. Their differential classes form a basis at $x$ by Step 2. Therefore the $n$ rows $\mathrm dF_1,\ldots,\mathrm dF_c,\mathrm dH_1,\ldots,\mathrm dH_d$ form a basis of $k^n$: the first $c$ are independent by the invertible minor, and the last $d$ are a basis modulo their span. The determinant $J$ of this square matrix is consequently nonzero in $k$.

source.place: Tag 01V7, lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth; Tag 02GU, lemma-etale-at-point, condition (8); Algebra 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth. The specified-coordinate square-Jacobian calculation.

proof.text: As a $C[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$-algebra, $A[1/J]$ has the presentation with variables $z_1,\ldots,z_n,w$ and relations $F_1,\ldots,F_c,H_1-T_1,\ldots,H_d-T_d,wJ-1$. Its square Jacobian determinant is $J^2$, up to sign: expand along the last column, whose only nonzero entry is $J$ in the last row. It is a unit. Thus [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] and [def-exc-jacobian-presentation] make this algebra etale over $C[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $c$ is etale on this open neighbourhood $U_0$ of $x$. Replace $U_0$ by $\bigcap_{g\in G}gU_0$, an invariant open containing $x$ and contained in $U_0$. Etaleness persists on this restriction by the local definition [def-weil-etale-morphism]. This gives the required pointed equivariant etale neighbourhood; the base is unchanged. Projection to $B$ is $h$ by Step 4. For $D=0$, $V=0$ and $d=0$; the same square-Jacobian argument proves that $h$ is etale near $x$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q90-27cbc74bf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item's 6 steps, the new node lem-per-local-cyclotomic-group-algebra-split, every cited statement, and ILO X Prop. 1.2 second assertion and X 1.3 (pp.136-140). The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to base. Steps 1-2: the geometric-point fixedness makes the actions k-linear on D, and delta is Lambda-linear and equivariant. The matrix units E^i_{ab} give an equivariant phi with k⊗V ≅ D; I checked the E_{a1}/E_{1a} block isomorphisms. Step 3 spreads out to an invariant open with no affineness assumption. Step 4 is the universal property of Sym. Step 5: the rows dF, dH form a basis by a dimension count from the cited Kähler-basis node, so 'elementary' is acceptable. Step 6: in the square presentation C[T][z,w]/(F,H-T,wJ-1), c+d=n, so it has n+1 equations in n+1 variables. Its determinant is J^2. The etale-presentation and ring/scheme nodes then apply, and the result is restricted to ∩gU_0. Avoiding ILO's radicial base change and its formula (4) is legitimate: (4) fails at a non-closed point fixed by C2 acting by (s,t)->(s,-t) on A^2. The new node is true (Brauer splitting plus a maximal order when |G| is invertible). I tested it on G=1, C2, S3 with N=6, Q8 with N=4, and p=0. Its form is correct (B1-B9). It does not restate the item. A search of all node statements for group algebra, group ring, Maschke, Brauer, splitting field, matrix units and cyclotomic found no duplicate; the nearest is lem-per-semisimple-algebra-matrix-division, which is the field case with division factors. There is no cycle. No SGA source is cited. The five declared off-unit tool_uses are generic black boxes and accepted.
